subject: merc
label: merc, in the place of the game's models/player/merc/merc.mdl

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/player/osrn-knight/osrn-knight.mdl, models/player/Aerocow-Trench/Aerocow-Trench.mdl, models/player/Gman_Black/Gman_Black.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps every bone, animation, attachment and bodypart of the base

M1.reason: Front, side, back and quarter views all read as a standing man in a jacket, trousers and boots, about the brief's height. Nothing sticks out or is missing. The sleeves are bulky and shapeless, but the outline is the one the brief describes.

M2.reason: Measured 26.7 x 27.2 x 69.6. The brief asks for about 69 tall, and 69.6 is within 1% of that. The width and depth are within the 15% band of the height-based size the brief gives.

M3.reason: Listing the brief's parts: jacket (present, olive, with sleeves), cargo trousers (present, but the thighs show no cargo pockets in the side, front or back views, so this small part is missing), two boots (present, brown), sunglasses (present, a black band across the eyes in the front and front-left views), gear pouches on the belt (present, two black pouches at the hips in the left, right and back-left views), hands (present as blocky mitts), head (present, with brown hair on top). Cargo pockets are missing, so M3 is at most 1. Separately, the back views (back, back-left, back-right) show small dark brown triangles on the back of each trouser leg just above the boot. They look like faces showing their back side or a boot part poking through, and they are not part of any item the brief names.

M4.reason: The brief names no colours, so the check is the materials it names: cloth jacket in olive green, cloth trousers in tan camo, leather-looking brown boots, skin on the face and hands, black glass or plastic on the sunglasses and pouches. Each region has one clear material and colour, and they agree with a mercenary's kit.

M5.reason: The brief's rough unshaven look is not there. The face in the front, front-left and front-right views is clean flat skin, with no stubble shading, no beard texture and no wear. The trousers have a horizontal camo stripe pattern and the jacket has a little shading, but nothing else the brief asks for is marked.

M6.reason: In the line-up (D, the green-jacketed figure), it sits next to three of Half-Life's own human models and is clearly cruder: blockier shoulders and sleeves, a flat-shaded head and no fine detail on the face or clothes. A player would see it as a different, lower-detail model rather than one of the game's own.

M7.reason: The front is the front: the sunglasses and face point to the viewer in the front view. It stands upright, with both boots on the floor line in the front, left and back views, and its origin is at the feet as a player model's is.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors, and 712 triangles is far under the 5,100 limit (twice the median of 2,550, which is higher than the 3,341 three-quarter mark). The measure passes, but the small dark triangles on the back of each trouser leg above the boot (back, back-left and back-right views) look like inside-out faces or a stray piece. The pictures cannot clear them as sound geometry, so this is one point below the measure.

C1.reason: In motion (run and dive frames), the parts stay on the body and the stride and reach look natural. But the far forearm in the run frames reads as a rigid bar held out in front, and the motion pictures show only our model, with no original to set against it. I cannot confirm from these frames that the arm stays attached through the swing, so this is one point below a full pass.

C2.reason: The contract is the player-model contract (every bone, animation, attachment and bodypart of the base). The harness measures it as kept, and the model's bones and animations play the dive and run in the pictures without any part detached. Measured fault count is zero, so there is nothing to cap this.
